title: [PDF] Molina Clinical Review Lumbar Spine MRI: Policy No. MCR-621

criteria.description: Documented trial of conservative therapy for at least 6 weeks ending within the last 6 months, consisting of inactive treatments (anti-inflammatory medications, activity modification, bracing, icing) plus at least one active treatment (physical therapy, chiropractic therapy, or provider-supervised home exercise program), with symptoms persisting, worsening, or not improving despite such care.
No same or similar imaging study recently completed without a specific documented reason for repeat imaging that will affect care.
Bowel or bladder dysfunction (decreased anal sphincter tone, urinary issues not due to stress incontinence) or saddle anesthesia documented on exam.

Progressive neurological deficit documented: weakness, abnormal reflexes, dermatomal sensory change, abnormal EMG/nerve conduction study indicating lumbar spine abnormality, or atrophy of related muscles.
Neurogenic claudication (pseudoclaudication) with x-ray showing significant lumbar spinal stenosis and intervention considered.
Scoliosis evaluation ordered by orthopedist or neurosurgeon with patient age and severity on x-ray indicating bracing or surgery may be provided.

Known or suspected tumor or mass: initial evaluation of recently diagnosed cancer, follow-up of known tumor/mass after treatment or with new signs/symptoms, surveillance per clinical standards, severe bone pain with history of cancer, or positive bone scan/x-ray suggestive of bone cancer.

criteria.description: Evaluation of spinal fractures or blunt trauma to the spine with abnormal neurologic findings.
Evaluation of spine abnormalities related to immune system suppression (e.g., HIV, chemotherapy, leukemia, lymphoma).
criteria.policy_citation: 5. Spine Issues Related to Immune System Suppression - https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/wa/Medicaid/resource/mcp-mcr/MCR-621-Lumbar-Spine-MRI.pdf

criteria.description: Suspected infection, abscess, or inflammatory disease with abnormal signs, symptoms, lab tests, or other imaging findings.
criteria.policy_citation: 6. Spine Issues Related to Infection or Other Inflammatory Process - https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/wa/Medicaid/resource/mcp-mcr/MCR-621-Lumbar-Spine-MRI.pdf

criteria.description: Congenital conditions: sacral dimples suspicious for dysraphism (skin lesions such as hairy patches, sacral lipomas, hemangioma, dimple >0.5 cm, or distance >2.5 cm from anal verge), known spinal dysraphism/spina bifida needing follow-up, or possible tethered cord.
Suspected ankylosing spondylitis with sacral iliac pain, elevated ESR or C-reactive protein, positive HLA-B27, or indeterminate x-ray result.
Known or suspected spinal vascular lesion or malformation.
